title: Core API — TotalCoin virtual wallet
description: Development of the Core API and microservices infrastructure for TotalCoin's virtual wallet and payment gateway platform.

problem.title: The Problem
problem.intro: TotalCoin's virtual wallet and payment gateway platform needed a robust transactional backend: a multi-level authorization flow for sensitive operations, with different business rules per sub-wallet, and infrastructure that stopped slowing down deployments.
items: Multi-level signer/approver flow with business rules differentiated per sub-wallet
Legacy microservices on .NET Framework 4.5 with slow, coupled deployments
Deployments that blocked shipping new functionality
The need to separate responsibilities without over-engineering

phases.title: 1. Business rules discovery
phases.description: Mapped the rules of the 4 commercial sub-wallets: who signs, who approves, in what order and with what amounts. Each sub-wallet had real, differentiated rules.
items: Multi-level authorization flow parameterized per sub-wallet
Limits and hierarchy rules documented before writing code
Differentiated business rules, not cosmetic ones

phases.title: 2. DDD and CQRS architecture
phases.description: Designed the module with Domain-Driven Design, separating commands from queries so writes and reads could evolve independently.
items: CQRS, Facade and Mediator patterns for separation of responsibilities
Domain aggregates (wallet, signer, approver, operation)
Well-bounded repositories and application services

phases.title: 3. Migration to Docker and Amazon ECS
phases.description: Migrated 3 critical legacy microservices (.NET Framework 4.5) into Docker containers deployed on Amazon ECS.
items: Architecture optimization with Docker containers
Amazon ECS as the microservices orchestrator
40% reduction in deployment time

phases.title: 4. Delivery and validation
phases.description: Validated the full flow against the business cases of all 4 wallets and stabilized operations in production.
items: Authorization flow tests for each business rule
Gradual rollout with zero monolith downtime
40% deployment time reduction measured on real releases

subsections.title: A modeled domain, not improvised
subsections.description: The authorization flow was modeled as part of the domain, with each wallet's rules as configurable policy instead of scattered conditionals.
items: Signer/approver chain with levels and amounts per wallet
Business rules isolated per wallet, reusing the common machinery
Traceability of every authorization decision

subsections.title: CQRS + Mediator to grow without breaking
subsections.description: Commands and queries separated with the Mediator pattern (via CQRS) so adding a wallet or a rule didn't recompile the whole flow.
items: Handlers per command: sign, approve, reject, cancel
State and audit queries decoupled from writes
Facade toward the wallet's internal clients

subsections.title: Microservices on Docker/ECS
subsections.description: The 3 most volatile microservices moved out of the monolith into containers, achieving independent deployments.
items: -40% deployment time from independent releases
Failure isolation: one service down doesn't take down the wallet
Per-service scaling based on real load

items.label: Domain first:
items.text: modeling each wallet's real rules before writing code avoided a mid-project redesign.

items.label: CQRS is not just a pattern:
items.text: separating commands from queries let audit and operational flows grow at different paces.

items.label: Containerizing pays off:
items.text: moving to Docker/ECS wasn't cosmetic: the -40% in deployment came from removing coupling to the monolith release.
